previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and a history of GAVE-related bleeding, was admitted for dyspnea on exertion and lightheadedness due to anemia. His hemoglobin had dropped to 7.5 g/dL, likely from ongoing upper gastrointestinal blood loss related to GAVE. He received two units of packed red blood cells in the emergency department with improvement in symptoms and a rise in hemoglobin to 9.3 g/dL. Cardiac and pulmonary evaluations were unremarkable, and his chronic right upper quadrant pain was attributed to known intestinal malrotation. His cirrhosis remained stable without signs of decompensation. He was discharged home in stable condition with continued management of his liver disease, GAVE prophylaxis, and instructions to follow up with his liver specialist.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male patient with HCC, requiring pre-operative
evaluation for TACE.

COMPARISON:  Prior chest CT from ___ and chest radiograph from
___.

TECHNIQUE:  PA and lateral chest radiographs.

FINDINGS:  Low lung volumes accentuate the bronchovascular structures and
cardiac silhouette.  There is mild bibasilar atelectasis.  There are no focal
consolidations, pleural effusions or pneumothorax. There are rib deformities
on the right. 

IMPRESSION:  No radiographic evidence of an acute cardiopulmonary process.

INDICATION:  ___ man with ___, please perform chemoembolization of the
liver.

PHYSICIANS:  Dr. ___ (radiology fellow) and Dr. ___
___ (radiology attending) who was present throughout and supervised the
procedure.

MEDICATION:  The procedure was performed under moderate conscious sedation,
the patient received 2 mg of Versed and 150 mcg of fentanyl for the total
intraservice time of 135 minutes, during which time the patient's hemodynamic
parameters were continuously monitored.  In addition, the patient received 30
mg of Toradol IV.

For chemoembolization, the patient received 60 mg of doxorubicin mixed with 20
mL of Lipiodol and 10 mL of Optiray. 10cc of intrarterial lidocaine was
administered.

PROCEDURES:
1.  Right common femoral artery access.
2.  Right hepatic artery angiography.
3.  Right hepatic artery cone-beam CT angiography.
5.  Lipiodol/doxorubicin TACE to segment V/VI.

CONTRAST:  140 mL Optiray 320.

RADIATION:  1823 mGy, 43.5 minutes of fluoroscopy time.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:

Following discussion of the risks, benefits and alternatives to the procedure,
informed written patient consent was obtained.  The patient was brought to the
angiographic suite and placed supine on the table.  A preprocedure timeout was
performed using three patient identifiers.  The skin of the right groin was
prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  

Approximately 5 cc of 1% lidocaine was infiltrated into the skin and
subcutaneous tissues for local anesthesia.  Using a combination of
fluoroscopic and palpatory guidance, a 21-gauge micropuncture needle was used
to access the common femoral artery.  An 018 nitinol wire was easily passed
through the needle which was then exchanged for a micropuncture sheath.  The
inner portion of the sheath and the wire were removed and exchanged for a
___ wire.  The micropuncture sheath was then exchanged for a 5 ___
___ Tip sheath, the sidearm which was continuously flushed with heparinized
saline throughout the procedure.  A 5 ___ C2 catheter was advanced over the
___ wire and positioned in the superior mesenteric artery.  SMA
angiography was performed at this point, which demonstrated a replaced right
hepatic artery arising directly from the SMA, the remainder of the mesenteric
branches were within normal limits. The portal vein was patent.  An 035
Glidewire was advanced through the C2 catheter into the replaced right hepatic
artery, the C2 catheter was removed and exchanged for a C2 glide catheter
which was positioned more distally in the right hepatic artery and repeat
angiography was performed.  This demonstrated two major branches within the
liver parenchyma, one passing superiorly towards the dome and one passing more
peripherally, this was accessed using a Glidewire and C2 catheter.  This
branch had two major branches within the liver parenchyma, both of these were
selectively accessed using a Fathom wire and Renegade ___ catheter. 
Contrast angiography performed in each of these vessels failed to demonstrate
a clear contrast blush indicating tumor supply; however a spin CT via the
right hepatic artery indicated that both vessels were supplying the region of
interest, therefore, we elected to perform chemoembolization via the main
trunk of this vessel, targeting segments V and VI.
A mixture of 60 mg of doxorubicin, 20 mL of Lipiodol and 10 mL of Optiray was
injected with intermittent injection of intra-arterial 1% lidocaine.  Once all
the doxorubicin had been administered, Gelfoam embolization was performed to
the trunk to near stasis.  The microcatheter and C2 catheter were removed.  An
angiographic run was performed at the access site demonstrating appropriate
level of access.  The sheath was removed and firm manual compression was
applied for 20 minutes, following which there was no further bleeding.  There
were no immediate post-procedure complications.

IMPRESSION:  
Technically successful semi selective chemoembolization of a segmental V/VI
branch of the right hepatic artery.
A mixture of 60 mg of doxorubicin, 20 mL of Lipiodol and 10 mL of Optiray was
injected.

HISTORY:  Status post TACE procedure.

TECHNIQUE:  CT of the abdomen without IV contrast.  Coronal and sagittal
reformats were reviewed.

COMPARISON:  MR from ___ and CT from ___.

FINDINGS:

The lung bases and cardiac apex are unremarkable.

Noncontrast appearance of the spleen, pancreas, bilateral kidneys and the
right adrenal is unremarkable.  The left adrenal is slightly obscured by large
splenic varices.  The stomach and imaged loops of large bowel as well as small
bowel are unremarkable.  Scattered abdominal lymphadenopathy is largely stable
from the prior exams.  The patient is status post cholecystectomy. Calcified
structure in the mid small bowel mesentery is stable and previously felt to
represent retained gallstones.

The patient is status post TACE with ethidiol uptake in the right lobe of the
liver including segment VII, VI and parts of V and VIII.   No extrahepatic
ethidiol uptake is demonstrated. The heterogenous appearance of the liver on
this non-contrast phase suggests underlying lesion, but is not fully
characterized here.

IMPRESSION:

Ethidiol uptake in the right lobe of the liver without evidence of
extrahepatic deposition.
